(2003) '''As assistant coach:''' * [[List of NBA G League champions|NBA G League champion]] (2018) }} '''James Alexander Singleton''' (born July 20, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and former assistant coach of the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]]. The 6'8" [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] played two years of college basketball for [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]]. ==College career== During his college career, Singleton, a graduate of [[Chicago]]'s [[Hirsch Metropolitan High School|Hirsch High School]], attended [[Pearl River Community College]] and [[Murray State University]]. In his two years at Murray State, he averaged 13.5 points, 10.5 rebounds and 1.9 [[block (basketball)|blocks]] in 60 games. He earned second-team All-[[Ohio Valley Conference]] honors in 2001–02 and first-team honors in 2002–03. He also led the OVC in rebounds as a senior. ==Professional career== Undrafted by an [[NBA]] franchise, Singleton began his professional career in [[Italy]] playing with the [[Aurora Basket Jesi|Sicc Cucine Jesi]] ([[LegADue|Lega2]]) during the 2003–04 season, averaging 20.8 points and 12 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game. He won the Lega2 title with his team which allowed Jesi there appear in Serie A. He also received Eurobasket All-Italian Lega2 Player of the Year award. He later signed with the [[Olimpia Milano]] ([[Serie A (basketball)|Serie A]]) team. He averaged 11.5 points, 8.6 rebounds and two steals in 46 games during the 2004–05 season, helping his team reach the Italian SerieA League Finals. He was named [[Most Valuable Player]] of the 2005 Italian League All-Star Game. During his tenure, Singleton was a fan favorite for his high-flying acrobatics and his tenacious defense. He was signed on August 30, 2005, by the Los Angeles Clippers to a two-year contract. This period marked his first appearance in the NBA. Singleton joined the [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|ACB]] for the 2007–08 season with [[Saski Baskonia|TAU Cerámica]]. He won the ACB title with this team, beating F.C. Barcelona in the Finals (3–0). Achieving success in Europe again Singleton returned for his second opportunity in the NBA as several teams took notice of his marked improvement. He would end up joining the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. On February 13, 2010, Singleton was traded from the [[Dallas Mavericks]] to the [[Washington Wizards]] along with [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]], [[Josh Howard]] and [[Quinton Ross]] for [[Caron Butler]], [[Brendan Haywood]], and [[DeShawn Stevenson]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/trade_100213.html|title=Wizards Acquire Howard, Gooden, Singleton, and Ross From Mavericks|work=NBA.com|date=February 13, 2010|accessdate=February 17, 2010}} On September 6, 2010, ''[[The Washington Post]]'' reported that Singleton had rejected a contract offer from the Wizards and signed with the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] in which he helped lead the team to the CBA finals.{{cite web |last=Lee |first=Michael |title=James Singleton leaves Wizards for China |work=The Washington Post |date=2010-09-06 |url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/wizardsinsider/2010/09/james-singleton-leaves-wizards.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006025032/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/wizardsinsider/2010/09/james-singleton-leaves-wizards.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 6, 2012 |accessdate=2010-09-08}} Singleton joined the Guangdong Southern Tigers for the 2011–12 season and helped lead the team to the CBA Finals. After the CBA season ended, he returned to the Washington Wizards.[http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards_sign_james_singleton_040512.html WIZARDS SIGN SINGLETON TO 10-DAY CONTRACT] Later in 2012, he returned to the Xinjiang Flying Tigers signing a two-year contract with the club.[http://www.niubball.com/2012/09/james-singleton-to-return-to-xinjiang-and-other-updates-on-cba-imports/ Urumqi reunion: James Singleton to return to Xinjiang (and other updates on CBA imports)] Taking time off from basketball for the birth of his son, Singleton was acquired by the [[Canton Charge]] on January 29, 2015.[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4921184 Charge Make Roster Moves] On May 8, he signed with [[Guaros de Lara (basketball)|Guaros de Lara]] of the Venezuelan [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto]] (LPB).[http://www.latinbasket.com/Venezuela/news/403784/Guaros-ink-James-Singleton Guaros ink James Singleton] On August 13, 2015, Singleton signed with [[Bnei Herzliya]] of the Israeli [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Ligat HaAl]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/172584/james-singleton-agreed-to-terms-with-bnei-herzliya.html|title=James
